evidence.note: Early explicit ordered plan articulated: '1. Check existing checkpoints. 2. Evaluate a couple to find best. 3. Check instruction datasets' and later 'create working eval script → evaluate checkpoints → if none hits 45%, launch SFT'. A clear staged plan matching anchor 5.

Risk-first sequencing: ran a `timeout 15` tiny training test (step133) to validate the training pipeline works end-to-end before committing compute, and built/tested the eval script on small `--limit 10` before scaling — an early cheap end-to-end pass (anchor 8 flavor).

Staged verification by information value: evaluated on 10→30→50→100→full 541 samples, doing expensive full-IFEval only on the most promising checkpoints. Baseline reproduced explicitly (base model 25.69% full, step180) as a done-check. Terminal 45% gate honored (46.03% full triggered writing best_checkpoint.txt).

Conditional go/no-go revision as results came in: on noticing SFT plateau/overfitting it launched continue-training, then Rank 128, then considered SDFT — plan adapted rather than repeating one run. But thresholds stayed loose/qualitative ('if not improving, change data') rather than crisp numeric per-stage gates.

A ~60-step stretch lost in a stuck-heredoc terminal loop shows the campaign was not a clean, sized milestone ladder; much mid-trajectory work was reactive checkpoint-fishing rather than a designed, budget-sized stage structure (below anchor 10).

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeded anchor 5: it had an ordered plan (get eval working → reproduce baseline → evaluate/fine-tune → iterate → 45% terminal check) with implicit done-checks, and reached into anchor 8 by validating the eval harness and training pipeline FIRST on tiny runs before scaling and by staging eval sample sizes from cheap to full by information value. However it falls short of 8-10 because per-stage success criteria were mostly implicit/qualitative rather than explicit numeric go/no-go thresholds, and the overall structure was emergent and reactive (including a long low-level detour) rather than a living, time-budget-sized milestone ladder. This places the observed behavior at a 6.
